questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Accessibility Testing”?
options: Accessibility Testing helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Accessibility Testing means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Accessibility Testing removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Accessibility Testing should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Accessibility Testing helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Accessibility Testing is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Keyboard-only testing” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Keyboard-only testing” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Keyboard-only testing” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Keyboard-only testing” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Keyboard-only testing” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Keyboard-only testing” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Keyboard-only testing” under Accessibility Testing. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Accessibility Testing”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
